results.content:
Calling a controller “supported” while an essential part of its jog-wheel behavior remains incomplete is extremely frustrating, especially when this limitation has already been reported and acknowledged.

I understand that automatically optimizing this behavior for every MIDI and HID controller may be difficult. However, VirtualDJ addresses this by exposing advanced parameters for jog behavior. Users can adjust scratch sensitivity, pitch-bend sensitivity, backspin after touch release, and the spin threshold separately.

Could djay Pro add an optional Advanced Jog Settings section with controls such as:

Backspin after touch release: On / Off

Backspin trigger threshold

Jog inertia gain

Inertia decay

Forward-spin continuation

Separate scratch and pitch-bend sensitivity [...] Hi @Billy\_T, welcome to the Community! Our team is still working on this. I’ll share more news here when I have it.

Experiencing this with my Rev5 as well. Love the software but the pitch bending thing when backspinning is a lingering annoyance. Any update on this?

Hi @somerandomdj, thanks for the feedback. We don’t have any updates to share yet regarding this. When I have more news, I will post it here. Thanks!

Title: Please add advanced jog-wheel inertia and backspin settings

The scratch response and overall jog-wheel feel in djay Pro are already excellent. I do not want to change the normal scratch sensitivity or response. [...] I am also frustrated because these controllers are listed as supported on the official djay website. When a controller is officially listed as supported, I expect the physical behavior of its jog wheels to be properly translated into the software—not merely for the buttons, faders, and basic scratch movement to function.

At the moment, the jog wheel and the software do not behave like a truly native integration. The physical platter may still be moving, but djay stops following that movement correctly after the touch signal is released. For a performance-oriented controller, accurate jog-wheel behavior is not an optional extra. It is one of the most fundamental parts of the controller.
